quote: All products are wheat-flour curry breads fried in a shared kitchen, so there is no gluten-free safe option.
found: /point/: 「当店で具材に合わせ、一から作った5種類 (カレーパン生地、食パン生地、トマト生地、黒生地、辛みの一味生地)の生地で包み込み」 and 「ブラックペッパーを混ぜたパン粉で揚げ」 — all five doughs are bread doughs, every one of the 15+ listed items is a fried panko-crumbed curry bread, and one (ホエー豚角煮) adds a 「そば衣」 coating. No allergen or gluten-free page exists on the site.
method: plain fetch of the cited root plus its three content subpages

quote: Signature items contain oysters (shellfish) and other varieties contain wagyu beef; breads are not plant-based.

quote: The grilled oysters are finished with soy-butter, miso-butter and lemon-soy-butter sauces, which use standard wheat-based Japanese soy sauce and miso.
found: The cited article's みやじま華屋敷 section says only 「王道の生牡蠣はもちろん、チーズベーコン牡蠣、レモン醤油バター牡蠣などの、変わった牡蠣メニューを楽しむことができます！」 — one of the three named sauces. The other two are evidenced elsewhere: rabico63 transcribes the board as 「しょう油バター 焼きがき 2個 ¥750 / みそバター 焼きがき 2個 ¥750」, and the Nohgaku Association guide says 「「みやじま華屋敷」の醤油バターや味噌バター」. The shop's own Threads/Instagram posts price 「醤油バター焼きガキ￥800」 and 「みそバター焼きガキ￥800」 and add 「味噌は色んな味噌をブレンドして作った特製味噌です」.
http: cited article 200 plain curl; Ecosia 200 (desktop UA); tabelog answered on s.tabelog.com with an iPhone UA after a 302 off tabelog.com
method: plain fetch of the cited page, then Ecosia search on the exact sauce names (Ecosia was the working engine this run)
note: Claim is true but over-reaches its citation — the hatsukaichi article names only レモン醤油バター. Repoint to the rabico63 menu transcript or the shop's own Instagram/Threads posts. Separately: tabelog lists the shop homepage as http://hanayashiki.bambina.jp/, now NXDOMAIN; the shop itself is trading (tabelog 10:00-19:00, reviews to 2025/11).

quote: Anago-meshi and the rice sets are seasoned with Japanese soy-sauce-based tare, which standardly contains wheat; no wheat-free seasoning is mentioned.
found: The cited /en homepage names the dishes but says nothing about seasoning. One click away, /en/menue1 ("restaurant menu", linked from the /en nav) states it outright: "purely domestic natural conger eel simmered in a sweet secret sauce on top of soy sauce rice cooked with a secret recipe" — repeated for the Conger eel set meal. The Japanese original (mirrored on umahiro.jp) reads 「秘伝のレシピで炊き込んだ醤油ご飯の上に甘めの秘伝タレで煮込んだ純国産天然アナゴ」.
http: 200 plain curl for /en, /en/menue1, /en/menue2, /en/menue3 (Wix site, server-rendered — no JS workaround needed)
method: plain fetch of the cited page, then its own menu subpages
note: Claim is true and stronger than recorded — the rice itself is 醤油ご飯 (soy-sauce-cooked), not just a tare on top — but the cited /en root does not carry it. Repoint to /en/menue1. Also gluten-relevant on that page and not yet recorded: フライ oysters, 穴子天丼-style tempura, and pork loin katsu, all wheat-crumbed.

quote: Menu is centered on conger eel and oysters with fish-based seasonings; no vegan or vegetarian items are listed.
found: Cited /en page: "'Anagomeshi set meal' using 'purely domestic natural conger eel', which is synonymous with Miyajima gourmet, You can enjoy 'oyster dishes' using 'pure Miyajima oysters' in meals and lunch boxes." The three menu subpages confirm the absence of any plant-based item: every listed dish is conger eel, clam, oyster, or pork cutlet, and even the school-trip bento carries momiji manju (egg/flour).
method: plain fetch of the cited page plus /en/menue1-3 to confirm the negative
note: Supported, with one over-claim to trim: nothing on the site says the seasonings are fish-based — the anago is described as simmered in a sweet secret tare over soy-sauce rice. Say 'soy-based seasonings' instead of 'fish-based seasonings'; the vegan verdict is unaffected.

quote: Anago rice and oyster bowls are seasoned with sweet soy-based tare/soy sauce, which in standard Japanese cooking is wheat-based.
found: On the cited page: a 2025/08 review headed 「ふっくら肉厚！秘伝のタレが染み込んだ至高のあなご料理✨」, and the operator's own PR text 「穴子飯やかき飯などの宮島伝統の味に加え…」. The soy attribution is confirmed one page deeper on the same listing, /dtlmenu/, which prints 「ほうれん草のしょうゆ麹ごま和え」 and 「ヨーグルトみそ漬け」 among the set-meal components.
http: tabelog.com 302 → s.tabelog.com, which returns 200 with an iPhone UA; the desktop host alone gives no usable body
method: iPhone-UA fetch of s.tabelog.com for the cited listing, plus its /dtlmenu/ subpage
note: Substance holds — the tare is on the cited page and 醤油麹/味噌 are named on its menu tab — but the cited page itself never says 醤油, so cite /dtlmenu/ alongside it. Two wording fixes: there is no oyster 'bowl' on the menu (it is かき飯定食), and the bigger untracked gluten sources are 穴子天丼 (tempura), カキフライ and かきのおかき揚げ. Also: the record's website field https://miyajimashokudo.jp/ is NXDOMAIN, and tabelog's listed homepage http://www.miyajima-shokudo.jp/menu.html is NXDOMAIN too; the only Wayback capture of miyajimashokudo.jp (2025-01-07) is the site of みやじま食堂別館, a different, mainland branch. The shop itself is trading (tabelog 公式, 無休 11:00-20:00, reviews and Instagram posts through 2026).

quote: All momiji manju are baked from a shared wheat-flour batter on the same griddle, so the entire product line contains gluten with no gluten-free preparation.
found: Cited article: 「こしあん・つぶあん・カスタードクリーム・チョコレート　120円／レーズン・クリームチーズ　130円」 — the whole product line — and of the plain bean-paste one, 「卵をたっぷり使ったカステラ生地と、甘さ控えめのあんこです」. The shop's own site (kimuraya-miyajima.com) lists the identical six plus a new 「おこもみじ」, 「広島の名産品であるお好み焼きともみじ饅頭を組み合わせたユニークなおやつ」.
http: 200 plain curl for the cited article; 200 plain curl for kimuraya-miyajima.com (Wix, server-rendered)
method: plain fetch of the cited page, then the shop's own site to confirm the current line-up
note: Substance holds — every item shares one カステラ生地 shell and there is no allergen or gluten-free page anywhere. Two wording fixes: the article never writes 小麦 (wheat is implied by カステラ生地, not stated) and it says nothing about a griddle, so drop 'on the same griddle'. Worth adding: the new おこもみじ is an okonomiyaki crossover, i.e. more wheat, not less.

quote: The batter is egg- and flour-based and fillings include dairy cream cheese, custard, and chocolate; bean-paste versions share the same egg-flour shell, so there is no vegan-safe item.
found: 「こしあん 卵をたっぷり使ったカステラ生地と、甘さ控えめのあんこです」 (the egg batter is described under the bean-paste variety itself) and 「デンマーク産ナチュラルクリームチーズを使用してあるとのことで、なめらかでコクのある味わい」, alongside the カスタードクリーム and チョコレート varieties in the price list.
method: plain fetch of the cited page
note: Fully supported, and precisely so — the cited article attaches the egg-heavy castella batter to the こしあん item specifically, which is the exact point a vegan reader would test. No change needed.

quote: The shop deep-fries wheat-batter momiji manju; there is no gluten-free menu and no published statement about a dedicated fryer, so cross-contamination should be assumed.
found: Cited /about/: 「紅葉堂のもみじまんじゅうのふんわりふっくらとしたカステラ生地に、料理人とともに試行錯誤し作り上げました独自の衣をまとわせ天ぷらにし、販売を開始し」, and the same page records 「平成18年　紅葉堂弐番屋をオープン…揚げもみじ®をはじめ…が、カフェスペースにて楽しめます」, so the statement is branch-specific. The wheat is spelled out on the same site: /zairyo 「小麦 瀬戸内の国産小麦100%に切り替え」, and momijido.com/pdf/allergy_2024.pdf lists 小麦粉 as a core ingredient of all six varieties. /agemomi/ describes the coating as 「揚げもみじ®専用生地」 mixed with water — a flour batter.
http: 200 plain curl for /about/, /zairyo, /agemomi/, /shop; the allergy PDF fetched 200 and read with pdftotext -enc UTF-8 -nopgbrk
method: plain fetch of the cited page, then the site's own ingredient page, shop page and allergy PDF
note: Supported and then some. Strengthen the citation with https://momijido.com/pdf/allergy_2024.pdf — it is a per-product allergen table with 小麦粉 ticked on every line, which is far better evidence than a company-history page, and it confirms there is no gluten-free variant to ask for.

quote: Cream and cheese fillings (dairy) are prepared in the same kitchen as the anko items, and the castella batter contains egg; no separation for vegan diners is documented.
found: Cited /about/: 「紅葉堂では、伝統のこしあんのほか、つぶあん、抹茶、クリーム、チョコレート、チーズを製造しており」 — one maker, one line, dairy and bean paste together. The egg half is on the same site rather than this page: /zairyo 「卵 純国産鶏「もみじ」の卵を100%使用…このもみじ卵を100%使用する事でたくさん空気を含んだカステラ生地ができ」, and the allergy PDF lists 卵 in every single variety including 【こしあん】 「あん（砂糖、小豆） 卵 砂糖 小麦粉 水あめ」.
http: 200 plain curl throughout; PDF via pdftotext -enc UTF-8 -nopgbrk
method: plain fetch of the cited page, then /zairyo and the allergy PDF for the egg claim
note: Supported, but cite the allergy PDF for the egg statement — /about/ does not mention egg. The PDF is also grounds for a tier change (see the vegan_status recommendation): egg is in the bean-paste item too, so nothing at this shop is vegan.

why: The operator's own allergen table lists 卵 in all six momiji manju varieties — 【こしあん】「あん（砂糖、小豆） 卵 砂糖 小麦粉 水あめ」 — so even the plain bean-paste item is not vegan, and クリーム/チョコレート/チーズ add 乳. /shop states Nibanya's entire range is 「揚げもみじ®、揚げもみソフト、ドリンクセット」, i.e. the fried manju plus a dairy soft serve. There is no plant-based item to have 'limited' access to.

quote: Food offerings (toast, morning set) use butter and egg; no dairy-free or vegan options are documented, so only black coffee is reliably plant-based.
found: Cited page, photo caption: 「ブレンドコーヒー450円と、トーストを両面鉄板で焼くバタートースト250円　※掲載時のデータです」. The article also records 「一昨年、2代目店主の夫・昭博（あきひろ）さんが病で倒れてからは、メニューを簡素化してほぼ一人で店に立っている」 — the menu has been cut back to essentially coffee and butter toast.
method: plain fetch of the cited page, then Ecosia to cross-check the shop's other coverage
note: Butter and the conclusion hold. Drop 'and egg' and 'morning set' — neither is on the cited page (卵/たまご/玉子/モーニング appear zero times in it). Do NOT import them from ことりっぷ's four-cafe roundup: the ハムエッグサンド with 玉子焼き there belongs to てらにし珈琲店 本店, a different shop in the same article. If the morning set matters, ことりっぷ does say 「今回紹介している4軒はすべてモーニングを提供している」 (2021, before the menu was simplified).

quote: Coffee is self-roasted and brewed nel-drip; plain black coffee is naturally gluten-free and vegan.
found: The cited page says the opposite of the roasting half: 「店内が想像できない外観。入り口左の大型焙煎機は昭博さんが倒れてから止まったままだ」 — the large roaster by the entrance has stood idle since the second-generation owner fell ill (the article dates that to 一昨年, i.e. ~2021; published 旅行読売 2023年8月号 / web 2023-10-16). Its only other roasting mention is historical: 「後年、失火で店の半分が焼け、豆の焙煎だけをしていた年もあったそうだ」. ネル and ドリップ appear zero times on the page.
http: 200 plain curl; Ecosia 200 for the cross-checks
method: plain fetch of the cited page, string-counted for ネル/ドリップ/自家焙煎/卵, then Ecosia for independent coverage
note: Two separate problems. (1) 'Self-roasted' is contradicted by the cited page — the roaster has been stopped for years; ことりっぷ's 2021 「貴重な焙煎機を使って、ていねいに直火焙煎された」 predates that and should not be used as current. (2) 'Nel-drip' is true but comes from elsewhere: note.com/hiroshima_coffee/n/n7aef72222508 (2024-06-04) has 「ネルドリップコーヒーを淹れながら穏やかに昔話をしてくださるのは店主の中村陽子さん」. Beware the same roundup trap as the vegan line — ことりっぷ's 「粗めに挽いた自家焙煎豆を、ネルドリップで…」 is about てらにし珈琲店, not 中村屋. Rewrite as 'coffee is brewed nel-drip (the in-house roaster has been out of use since the owner's illness)' and cite the note.com piece. Shop is trading: japanhomeycafes.com (2026-01) and note.com both give 11:00-16:00, closed Sun-Tue, matching the cited article.

quote: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki uses a wheat-flour batter and wheat noodles cooked on a shared teppan griddle, making cross-contact with gluten unavoidable.
found: Cited root: 「お好み焼き 鉄板焼き ねぎ庵 流川店」, 「素材・麺・ねぎにこだわり鉄板焼メニューが自慢のねぎ庵」, 「手作りの鉄板自家製料理」, and 「ボリューム満点の鉄板・お好み焼きコース…4500円以上のコースからは、焼きそばが食べ放題！！」 — okonomiyaki, noodles and everything else on one teppan.
method: plain fetch of the cited root plus its own /foods menu
note: Supported. /foods makes it worse in a useful way: every okonomiyaki carries イカ天 (wheat-battered squid tempura), そば/うどん are swap options and paid doubles, and 広島名物 includes がんす (crumbed fried fishcake). Nothing on the site mentions allergens or a separate cooking surface.

quote: Teppanyaki and okonomiyaki dishes are seasoned with standard sauces and soy sauce, which contain wheat.
found: The cited root never mentions sauce or soy sauce. Its own /foods page does: toppings 「中マヨor外マヨ/ピリ辛ソース 各55円」 and 「激辛ソース/からしマヨ 各77円」; 「焼きおにぎり 各440円(税込) (醤油バター、チーズ、明太マヨ、梅しそ)」 names soy sauce outright; and 「塩マヨとんぺい…オタフクアイデアコンテスト全国 第1位 獲得！」 ties the kitchen to Otafuku, the wheat-containing okonomiyaki sauce.
method: plain fetch of the cited root, then the site's own /foods menu
note: True but cited to the wrong page on the right site — repoint to https://negian.owst.jp/foods, which names ソース, 醤油バター and the Otafuku connection explicitly.

quote: Dishes are prepared on a shared griddle with pork, egg, oysters, and beef, so vegan separation is not provided.
found: The cited root evidences only the oysters and the shared teppan (「広島産牡蠣やこだわりの素材」, 「【牡蠣の鉄板焼き】牡蠣とキノコ焼き 968円」). All four proteins are on /foods: pork (「豚キムチ」, 「せんじがら」, とんぺい, 「肉玉そば」), egg (「たまごW」, 「月見ねぎ庵スペシャル」, 「オムレツ焼きそば」), oysters (「広島県産かき 550円」, 「かきホーレン」, 「かきの酒蒸し」) and beef (「和牛コーネ 1,133円」, 「牛すじ煮込み 693円」).
method: plain fetch of the cited root, then the site's own /foods menu
note: Claim is right; repoint to /foods, which itemises all four. The plant-looking items are traps worth recording: 大根梅サラダ, 枝豆, トマトスライス and the 漬物 are the only candidates, and everything else on the board shares the same griddle.

quote: An English menu is available, which helps travelers identify ingredients before ordering.
found: Cited root, 詳細情報 → 設備: 「英語メニュー あり」, and the page header carries a live switcher 「language 日本語 English 한국어 中文(繁体字) 中文(简体字)」. /en/foods renders the full board in English with per-item components, e.g. "[Staff Recommendation] Mayo Special … Medium mayonnaise, squid tempura, egg W".
method: plain fetch of the cited root, then the English menu it links to
note: Supported, but add a warning to the positive rather than leaving it bare: the English menu lists dish components, not allergens, and it renders そば as "soba" — "Meat and egg soba", "Yakisoba (Udon)" — which in Hiroshima okonomiyaki is wheat ramen noodle, not buckwheat. A celiac reading 'soba' as buckwheat here would be badly misled, so the English menu is a navigation aid, not a safety aid.
